content.value_statement: TypeScript teams need reliable PostgreSQL connection patterns for Azure Flexible Server. This skill provides focused node-postgres examples for authentication, pooling, queries, transactions, and token refresh.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install pg, @azure/identity, and TypeScript typings.
Provides password and Microsoft Entra ID authentication examples.
Demonstrates Client and Pool connection patterns for node-postgres.
Explains parameterized queries, transactions, and typed query results.
Includes an Entra ID token refresh pool wrapper for long-running services.
Covers PostgreSQL error handling, SSL settings, and pool sizing guidance.
limitations: Does not provision Azure PostgreSQL servers or databases.
Does not verify connectivity against a live Azure environment.
Requires users to supply valid database credentials or managed identity configuration.
Focuses on node-postgres and does not cover ORM-specific patterns.

use_cases.title: Create a Secure Database Client
use_cases.description: Use the examples to configure pg Client or Pool settings for Azure PostgreSQL with SSL enabled.

use_cases.title: Move to Passwordless Authentication
use_cases.description: Adapt the Entra ID token examples for managed identity based PostgreSQL access.

use_cases.title: Standardize Query Patterns
use_cases.description: Reference the parameterized query and transaction sections when reviewing TypeScript data access code.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Basic Connection
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new TypeScript service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect a TypeScript Node.js service to Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server using pg and environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Production Pool
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production-ready pg Pool configuration for Azure PostgreSQL with SSL, timeouts, and graceful shutdown.

prompt_templates.title: Use Entra ID Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to connect to Azure PostgreSQL from TypeScript using DefaultAzureCredential and an Entra ID access token.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Transaction Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable TypeScript transaction helper for pg that supports typed results, rollback, and connection release.

output_examples.input: Request a password-based Azure PostgreSQL connection pattern.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan with required packages, environment variables, SSL configuration, connection lifecycle, and cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: Ask for safe query examples for user records.
output_examples.output: Parameterized query guidance that explains placeholders, parameter arrays, typed results, and why string concatenation should be avoided.

output_examples.input: Ask how to refresh Entra ID tokens in a long-running service.
output_examples.output: A pool management approach that refreshes tokens before expiry, closes stale pools, and reuses the active pool when valid.

best_practices: Use parameterized queries for all user-controlled values.
Use connection pools with explicit shutdown handling in production services.
Prefer Microsoft Entra ID authentication when the Azure deployment supports managed identity.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate user input into SQL statements.
Do not disable Azure PostgreSQL SSL certificate verification.
Do not hardcode database passwords or connection strings in source files.

faq.question: Does this skill create an Azure PostgreSQL server?
faq.answer: No. It explains TypeScript connection patterns for an existing Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server.

faq.question: Which Node.js package does it use?
faq.answer: It uses pg, also known as node-postgres, with optional @azure/identity support.

faq.question: Does it support passwordless authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Microsoft Entra ID examples using DefaultAzureCredential and PostgreSQL access tokens.

faq.question: Can I use these examples in production?
faq.answer: Yes, after adapting credentials, network rules, pool sizing, error handling, and deployment settings for your environment.

faq.question: Does it cover SQL injection prevention?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes parameterized queries and shows placeholder-based query patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover ORMs like Prisma or TypeORM?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on direct node-postgres usage in TypeScript applications.
